nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: It was then submerged in a solution containing 0.708 g of nickel nitrate hexahydrate (Ni(NO3)2·6H2O), 0.72 g of urea, and 0.21 g of ammonium fluoride in a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave. The autoclave was sealed and maintained at 120 °C for 6 hours, enabling the formation of Ni(OH)2 via a hydrothermal reaction.

nodes.name: Spray modification with PA and Fe
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, a handheld spray gun was used to evenly spray phytic acid solution (6%) and FeCl3 solution (50 mM) onto the surface of the Ni(OH)2 sample at amounts of 10 μL cm−2 and 20 μL cm−2, respectively. The sample was then rinsed with deionized water and dried, resulting in the preparation of the Ni(OH)2–PA–Fe nanosheet array.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Ni(OH)₂ exhibit distinct peaks at 19.2°, 33.5°, 39.0° and 60.1°, corresponding to the (001), (100), (101) and (110) planes of the Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDS no. 97-005-3993). Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe reveals no additional characteristic peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Fig. S1†, the XRD patterns of the synthesized Ni(OH)₂ exhibit distinct peaks at 19.2°, 33.5°, 39.0° and 60.1°, corresponding to the (001), (100), (101) and (110) planes of the Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDS no. 97-005-3993).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image reveals Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets with smooth surfaces uniformly distributed across NF substrate. Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe nanosheet array exhibits small burrs due to deposition of iron phytate complex.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM image (Fig. S2†) reveals that the Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets with smooth surfaces are uniformly distributed across the NF substrate. In comparison, the nanosheet array of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe (Fig. 1a) exhibits small burrs because of the deposition of the iron phytate complex.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of Ni(OH)₂ shows lattice fringe spacing of 0.262 nm corresponding to (100) plane. Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe shows increased porous structures and lattice fringe spacing of 0.233 nm indexed to (101) facet, retaining well-defined crystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The evident lattice fringe spacing of 0.262 nm corresponds to the (100) plane of Ni(OH)₂ (Fig. S3†). ... Regarding the HRTEM of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe in Fig. 1c, the lattice fringe spacing of 0.233 nm can be indexed to the (101) facet of Ni(OH)₂, demonstrating that the catalyst retains a well-defined crystalline structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM combined with EDX elemental mapping illustrates uniform distribution of Ni, O, Fe, P and C elements throughout Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) combined with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping (Fig. 1d) illustrates the presence and uniform distribution of Ni, O, Fe, P and C elements throughout the nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe shows peaks at 3440-3680 cm⁻¹ (O–H stretching), 990 cm⁻¹ and 1070 cm⁻¹ (P–O, P–O–C), and broad peak at 1140 cm⁻¹ (P=O), confirming iron phytate attachment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 3440-3680 cm⁻¹ are assignable to the O–H stretching vibrations associated with the Ni(OH)₂ structure and interlayer water molecules. Compared to Ni(OH)₂, the peaks at 990 cm⁻¹ and 1070 cm⁻¹ and the broad peak centred at 1140 cm⁻¹ in the FTIR spectra of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe are assigned to the stretching vibrations of the P–O, P–O–C, and P=O bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe exhibits zeta potential of -16.8 mV, Ni(OH)₂–PA -14.5 mV, Ni(OH)₂–Fe -5.2 mV, confirming more negatively charged surface layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2b, Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe exhibits a negative zeta potential of -16.8 mV, compared to zeta potentials of -14.5 mV for Ni(OH)₂–PA and -5.2 mV for Ni(OH)₂–Fe, which confirms the successful formation of a more negatively charged layer on the catalyst surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS mapping shows prominent PO₃⁻ detection on Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe surface, indicating phytic acid phosphate groups envelope.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As visibly shown in Fig. 2c, PO₃⁻ is prominently detected on the surface of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe, indicating that the catalyst surface is enveloped by phytic acid with phosphate groups.

nodes.characterization_summary: P 2p XPS of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe shows peaks at 133.6 eV (M–O–P bond) and 134.7 eV (P–O bond). Ni 2p₃/₂ shows Ni²⁺ peaks at 855.6 eV and 873.3 eV, Ni³⁺ at 857.4 eV and 875.2 eV with 0.18 eV negative shift compared to Ni(OH)₂. Fe 2p shows peaks at 712.3 eV and 725.5 eV with pre-peak at 706.7 eV indicating lower oxidation state Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution P 2p spectra (Fig. 2d), the peak at a binding energy of 133.6 eV is attributed to the M–O–P bond, while the peak at 134.7 eV can be ascribed to the P–O bond... As observed in the high-resolution Ni 2p₃/₂ spectra (Fig. 2e), the strong peaks at binding energies of 855.6 and 873.3 eV can be assigned to Ni²⁺, and the peaks at 857.4 and 875.2 eV correspond to Ni³⁺... Notably, the Ni 2p₃/₂ peak of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe shows a negative shift of 0.18 eV compared with Ni(OH)₂. Regarding the Fe 2p spectra of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe in Fig. S4a†, a pair of peaks at binding energies of 712.3 and 725.5 eV... are assigned to Fe 2p₃/₂ and Fe 2p₁/₂, respectively. In addition, a low-intensity peak at 706.7 eV... is attributed to the presence of Fe ions in a lower oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR spectra of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe exhibit more pronounced symmetrical signal of oxygen vacancies at g ≈ 1.99 than Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 2f, the ESR spectra of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe exhibit a more pronounced symmetrical signal of oxygen vacancies at g = ∼1.99 than that of Ni(OH)₂, proving that Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe possesses rich oxygen vacancy defects due to its porous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS of Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe shows P–O bond in P 2p confirming stable phytate layer presence. Ni 2p shows increased Ni³⁺ proportion indicating NiOOH formation. Fe 2p shows slight shift to higher binding energy indicating increased Fe valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 5d, the P–O bond was observed in the P 2p spectrum, indicating the stable presence of the phytate layer... As illustrated in Fig. 5e, the high-resolution XPS spectra of Ni 2p in Ni(OH)₂–PA–Fe show an increased proportion of Ni³⁺ peaks... Similarly, the Fe 2p spectra (Fig. 5f) display a slight shift towards higher binding energy, indicating an increase in the Fe valence state after the OER.
